title: Economy: 26 Oct 2026
key_takeaways: The Fed held at 5.25-5.50%; dot plot signals two 25bp cuts in 2027 contingent on inflation easing to 2%.
The RBA held at 4.35% with a mild tightening bias; markets price the first cut in Q2 2027 after Q4 CPI.
US 10-year yields at 4.38%; AU 10-year at 4.55%; AUD/USD near 0.6480, lower end of 3-month range.

sections.1_economy:
## United States

The Federal Open Market Committee held the federal funds rate at 5.25-5.50% at its 1 November 2026 meeting. The post-meeting statement retained data-dependent language. The September dot plot showed a median of two 25bp cuts in 2027, contingent on PCE inflation falling to 2.1% or below.

Q3 2026 GDP came in at 2.1% annualised (BEA advance estimate), below the 2.4% consensus but consistent with a soft landing. September CPI was 3.1% year-on-year; core PCE was 2.7%, still above the 2% target. Non-farm payrolls added 192,000 in September (BLS); unemployment was 4.1%.

Markets are pricing approximately 40bp of cuts by end-2027, slightly less than the dot plot implies. The main dissenting view - held by two FOMC members - is that rates should hold at 5.50% until core PCE is sustainably below 2.5%.

## Australia

The Reserve Bank of Australia held the cash rate at 4.35% at its October 2026 meeting. The statement noted inflation is returning to target but at a slower pace than forecast. Governor Bullock signalled the Board will not act before seeing another full quarterly CPI print, ruling out a move before February 2027.

Q3 CPI came in at 3.8% year-on-year (ABS); trimmed mean was 3.5%, still above the 2-3% band. Unemployment edged to 4.3% in September. Markets price the first 25bp cut in May 2027 (OIS pricing). The consensus of major bank economists is two cuts in H2 2027, taking the cash rate to 3.85% by year-end.

## Outlook and scenarios

**Base case:** Fed executes 50bp of cuts in 2027; RBA begins cutting mid-2027. US growth stays positive but sub-trend; Australia avoids recession. AUD/USD holds 0.64-0.67.

**Scenario 1 - Faster easing:** If US core PCE falls to 2.2% by February 2027, the Fed could cut 75bp, pulling global yields lower and supporting risk assets. AUD/USD could rally toward 0.70.

**Scenario 2 - Inflation re-accelerates:** US services inflation stalling above 3.5% could reprice to zero Fed cuts. US 10-year yields would move toward 4.7-4.8%, widening credit spreads and slowing deal activity.

**Scenario 3 - RBA hikes:** If Q4 trimmed mean CPI comes in above 3.8%, the RBA could deliver a 25bp hike in February 2027 - a significant surprise. AUD/USD would spike briefly before broader risk-off offsets gains.
